Appears to be a well made dishwasher. Time will tell! The second time I used it there was a bit of water on the floor in the front. After researching the manual I discovered the two rubber ports leading to the drip tray. Yes I should have noticed them in the instruction manual. BUT, there is really not too much info on what happens if you find water on the floor in the front of the dishwasher. To make a long story short I believe I had used the sink while the dishwasher was running causing too much water to be pumped out during the rinse cycle. I watched the two ports to see if there was any dripping/water flow into the drip pan or if any other connections were leaking. PROBLEM WAS RESOLVED. Lessoned learned! MAKE SURE the garbage disposal is cleared and you don't add any excess water during the cycle. I like the front controls feature also. The first few times I would accidently hit one of the buttons but again practice makes perfect.

They "fixed" that and the dishwasher worked for a few months and is now no longer connecting to WiFi, not a big deal, but a nice feature, the auto release is not working again and the full rinse aid light is constantly on even though the rinse aid compartment is full. Of course it's just outside the warranty date and the extended warranty company is refusing to fix it since it's a replacement unit, even though they confirmed they would prior to replacement.

Sentence (English): We are really enjoying our oven - we've had it for about a month and have already utilized the double ovens multiple times.
Comments (English): We are really enjoying our oven - we've had it for about a month and have already utilized the double ovens multiple times. For someone without space for wall ovens, this is a great alternative. Additionally, having the smaller spaces seems to bring ovens to temp quickly. There is ample cook space, especially with adjustable burner sizes. The lower oven could be a challenge for some since it is closer to the ground and the larger of the two, but so far a non-issue for us. The knobs for both burners and ovens are not entirely intuitive yet, there are quite a few options one each but this is just getting used to a new thing. The LG app is surprisingly helpful. Manuals & a chat help feature are right there. Having it connected to WiFi is new, but helpful. We also purchased an LG over range microwave at same time, so I've used the app a little more often.The double tap to turn on the interior lights is a handy feature, especially with the blue interior. Makes it easy to view food without letting heat out. Reasons for only 4 stars - minor-ish but…enough for me to remove a star.1. Cook top knobs turn the burners on too easily if bumped into while working in kitchen. It's fairly easy to notice, but it's a concern. If the dog misbehaves, as they sometimes do, I think they could accidentally turn a burner on. But they're never home alone outside their crate so for us that isn't as likely of a problem as it could be. We also do not have little ones in the house often at this time. If we don't adjust and stop accidentally turning a few on, we may buy child proof covers. Hopefully not, they wouldn't be very aesthetically pleasing. 2. The chime is quite long, louder than I prefer and cannot be adjusted - volume, length or melody. Only way is to turn off all sound on panel - which I tried and the beeps when pressing buttons are too helpful for me. This is same for microwave as well - chat feature on app helped me determine this was the case for both. 3. The legs do not go high enough to make level with our counter. It's just a 1/4 inch or so, not super noticeable but it's there. It may just be something odd with our flooring or maybe our counters are an odd height? But it feels like the legs would be long enough to allow for this.Delivery & customer service - the delivery staff were very friendly and let me vacuum and clean quickly before installing new appliances.Late arrival - which happens, but was more frustrating as tracking link kept stating two stops ahead, estimated delivery time did not change until estimated arrival windows passed and increased significantly. Received call 1 minute before delivery window closed - was supposed to be ****-****. Arrived at 1330, did not leave until 1800 - VERY long day. Reason customer service gave when calling was obviously dishonest and accidentally confirmed by delivery staff.Due to late arrival and length of installation I ended up not being able to actually work from home most of the day. I have a super flexible schedule and minimal calls scheduled that day so wasn't as big of an issue for me as it could have been for others. But 9 hours is a long time. On top of that…the delivery staff was in a rush, obviously, and left with frustrating issuesInstalled over range microwave after/during installing stove. Did not cover cooktop when installing over range. Left sawdust on oven and counters. Sawdust and larger pieces of debris are STILL coming out of microwave and I am still dealing with Home Depot over it. It is still dropping into the air intake on back of stove and I'm concerned about it affecting the ovens and scratching cooktop. I've vacuumed and cleaned everything I can multiple times and it's still happening. The “48-hours” return window is causing me some issues as this is ongoing and not receiving much assistance. Was surprised with the mess left behind overall. Manuals and accessories basically dumped on my island, surprised fridge filters were not installed, found out after they left. 3 appliances removed, one relocated and the relocated refrigerator into garage was not actually moved in place - left a few feet away from space and we moved into place and plugged in. Had to move one vehicle in front of garage and clear out separate part of garage - not really an issue except they had old appliances and the delivery trucks sitting behind said car so I was on “standby” for almost an hour to jump up and finally move vehicle after originally asked to do it “real quick”. I'd also ensured over half of the garage was completely clear where the fridge was going, thought I'd over compensated but they would not take fridge into garage the way I expected, even though they could have - we moved freezer in same way.They also very unceremoniously folded and shoved a large & expensive area rug out of the way and also stacked items on it. I'd already moved rug completely out of kitchen area - was shocked to find it moved and unrolled with tools and parts stacked on it. Used island and countertops as a workspace with no surface protection. Again, using surfaces would be expected but not protecting them and/or cleaning up after was not cool.Contacted Home Depot after delivery and noticing most issues. They proved a few small credits - it was somewhat quick but had to negotiate quite a bit and am still unhappy. They offered to reinstall a few items brand new BUT issues that warranted it were not apparent until after the call and 48 hours. Additionally - I was not looking forward to another 9 hour day. We spent $10,000 on our package - fridge and dishwasher were where I truly indulged and didn't find an induction oven I was excited about. Anyways….regardless of how much we spent, shocked that Home Depot has yet to make things right.All 4 appliances are fantastic - delivery & install worst part, which isn't end of world usually and mostly expected. But it is still causing issues. The actual install, outside of the ongoing sawdust issue was great. I could tell the lead knew what they were doing in that regard. And really nice and polite.

On top of that…the delivery staff was in a rush, obviously, and left with frustrating issuesInstalled over range microwave after/during installing stove. Sentence (English): We like the Eco Series front door style and flush face with angled controls easy to access and see with our overhanging counter.
Comments (English): [ Does not Dry Well and Drips - So its Just OK ] || ---------------- || We like the Eco Series front door style and flush face with angled controls easy to access and see with our overhanging counter. The door finish looks nice, and the door is solid. The small upper third rack is A-OK for our use for silverware, small items, and a few larger tools in the deeper middle space. It is quiet as advertised. We were told by a rep at the other home handyman store that this is their most popular dishwasher but now we wonder if we couldn't have done better. The soap door does not stay shut so already have a service call. The insulation does not stay on well while placing the washer. The standard wash cycle took a long time - 2.5 hours. After the dry cycle, when the door is opened the back of the door is covered with moisture, and on both sides of the door drips on our wood floors. With a deep well in the door, it becomes a puddle and has to be hand dried or just shut the door with water going into the main space. Plastic storage containers are more wet than with our failed old Electrolux washer. The little vent at the top of the door might or might not do anything, but it retains water, which drips out and will put some water stain on the back of the door over time. So, the washer is "just OK" and we wonder if Whirlpool/KitchenAid tested this washer in a home setting before releasing it.

Comments (English): The LG dishwasher's air filter is a very useful feature that further enhances the performance of the dishwasher. The air filter purifies the air and quickly removes moisture remaining after washing, allowing you to leave the dishwasher feeling refreshed. Secondly, this filter also filters out fine dust and bacteria in the air, keeping the interior of the dishwasher clean. This plays an important role in enhancing the hygiene of the dishwasher. In addition, since the filter continuously purifies the air, it prevents unpleasant odors that may occur during washing. The air filter is automatically cleaned, providing convenience to the user. It is a big advantage that it reduces the user's hands, as there is no need to clean or replace the filter separately. In addition, it is effective in preventing mold and bacteria growth by not leaving moisture inside the dishwasher. Thanks to the air filter, every time you use the dishwasher, there will be no food residue or odor after washing, allowing you to use clean and refreshing dishes. The addition of this filter further enhances the performance of the dishwasher and maintains a hygienic environment, providing a satisfactory user experience. The air filter in your LG dishwasher is an essential feature that helps keep your dishes clean at home.

Sentence (English): Absolutely the worst experience ever with having a dishwasher delivered and installed.

Hopefully someone will return one of my multiple messages and refund me for service that didn't happen.

Hopefully someone will return one of my multiple messages and refund me for service that didn't happen.

I love how it gets every dish clean and nothing has to be washed before going into the dishwasher. They need to include in the instructions the different sizes of hookups, we had to go to the hardware store and buy a couple extra pieces, but was not sure on the sizes. Controls: the instructions are not especially complete or clear either for the wifi setup or for use of the manual selections. Full access to controls requires a wifi network and phone. Unless you just love to have remote control of your dishwasher, this seems both intrusive and not fully explained. For example there is no rinse and hold button. Most problematic is the lack of timely customer support. I waited 45 minutes and gave up on my first attempt. The second time I was forced to select the wifi support option and the tech seemed unable to answer my questions about operations and dropped the call mid-stream without a followup . Not good.

Sentence (English): Excels at cleaning dishes but the lack of user interface is catastrophic.
Comments (English): [ High performing but unusable ] || ---------------- || Excels at cleaning dishes but the lack of user interface is catastrophic. A majority of the dishwasher controls are only available via the app - things like eco, half load, delay start. And the indicator that the dishwasher cycle is complete - a single LED - turns off 10 minutes after the cycle ends. The lack of controls and feedback on the device itself make this a major pain to share dishwasher responsibilities as a household, especially if not everyone is using the app (like kids or houseguests). It's absurd that I had to buy a little clean/dirty magnet that I manually change twice a day instead of this expensive product displaying it automatically. This mitigation helps me live with this dishwasher I was already stuck with, but I absolutely would not have bought this had I realized what a pain this would be. Pros are: really good cleaning power (never rinse anything, even gets baked on food which I thought was a myth), lots of settings (in the app only though), Wi-Fi is nice to have and integration with smart home functionality for voice commands (and on a Google Home display, the voice command even pulls up some cycle options - though not all of them). I would consider another Bosch for these reasons but only after thoroughly evaluating the product is functional without relying on an app.

Sentence (English): It turns out to be a practical and reliable dishwasher, with some advantages that are really noticeable in everyday life.
Comments (English): [ Practical and efficient for the home ] || ---------------- || It turns out to be a practical and reliable dishwasher, with some advantages that are really noticeable in everyday life. What I would highlight the most is that it is very easy to use, with an intuitive control panel and programs that adapt to different needs, such as the quick cycle when you need something clean in a short time. The stainless steel finish not only looks modern, but is also easy to clean, which is a plus. Also, I like that the machine is quite quiet; you can run it at night without worrying about the noise. The drying system is efficient, although with the plastics sometimes a drop of water remains, which seems common in many dishwashers. The connectivity with the Home Connect app is interesting, but I have used it little; it is useful if you want to receive notifications or control the dishwasher from the sofa, but not essential for everyone. As for consumption, it is noticeable that it uses less water and energy compared to older models I have had, which is a relief for the pocket and the environment. The only drawback I could point out is that the normal cycles can be a bit long, but at least the cleaning result is impeccable. Overall, I am very satisfied with this dishwasher. It is a good investment if you are looking for something that is efficient, modern and makes household chores easier.

Sentence (English): On November 30th we bought a Whirlpool dishwasher and combination microwave/range hood from Lowe's.
Comments (English): [ Demand experienced installers ] || ---------------- || On November 30th we bought a Whirlpool dishwasher and combination microwave/range hood from Lowe's. We paid $169 to install the D/W and $129 to install the M/W. An outside company was to make the delivery and do the installation. When the installer came he said he couldn't handle the M/W because the kitchen backsplash is granite. He didn't feel comfortable in drilling a hole in the granite, thinking he might crack it. So he set about working on the D/W. He removed our old D/W and put in the new one. After he did that he noticed the new D/W was damaged; he called Lowe's to complain. They said they would give us another new one. We told the installer to put our old D/W back which was now in our garage; but he said if he did that he'd have to charge us an additional $169. We weren't about to pay two fees for one D/W. We resigned ourselves to doing without a D/W for the next few weeks. After the installer left we realized he hadn't reconnected the drain pipes under the sink. We found this out because water drained out onto the kitchen floor. We were unable to use the right side sink at all; we could only use the left side. All this could have been avoided had the installer simply examined the D/W when he took it out of the box and looked for damage. We really wanted the D/W since we were having a large dinner party; but we ended up doing all the dishes by hand in one side of our sink! We feel Lowe's should have used their influence with the installation company to move us up as a priority rather than making us wait an additional three weeks. As for the M/W, it is sitting in the box in our garage. We are still looking for an experienced handyman to do the installation. Lowe's did credit us for the $129 installation fee. The new D/W works fine.

Sentence (English): It turns out to be a practical and reliable dishwasher, with some advantages that are really noticeable on a day-to-day basis.
Comments (English): [ Practical and efficient for the home ] || ---------------- || It turns out to be a practical and reliable dishwasher, with some advantages that are really noticeable on a day-to-day basis. What I would highlight the most is that it is very easy to use, with an intuitive control panel and programs that adapt to different needs, such as the quick cycle when you need something clean in a short time. The stainless steel finish not only looks modern, but is also easy to clean, which is a plus. Also, I like that the machine is quite quiet; you can run it at night without worrying about the noise. The drying system is efficient, although with the plastics sometimes a drop of water remains, which seems common in many dishwashers. The connectivity with the Home Connect app is interesting, but I have used it little; it is useful if you want to receive notifications or control the dishwasher from the sofa, but not essential for everyone. As for consumption, it is noticeable that it uses less water and energy compared to older models I have had, which is a relief for the pocket and the environment. The only drawback I could point out is that the normal cycles can be a bit long, but at least the cleaning result is impeccable. Overall, I am very satisfied with this dishwasher. It is a good investment if you are looking for something that is efficient, modern and makes household chores easier.

Además, me gusta que la máquina sea bastante silenciosa; puedes ponerla a funcionar por la noche sin preocuparte por el ruido.El sistema de secado es eficiente, aunque con los plásticos a veces queda alguna gota de agua, lo que parece común en muchos lavavajillas. El único inconveniente que podría señalar es que los ciclos normales pueden ser algo largos, pero al menos el resultado de limpieza es impecable.En general, estoy muy satisfecho con este lavavajillas. Es una buena inversión si buscas algo que sea eficiente, moderno y que facilite las tareas del hogar.

Reason for Purchase: Since I live in a rented apartment, I couldn't buy a built-in model, so I purchased this one. It is a 25-pyeong (approx. 82 sq ft) unit, so I bought it to use in a small space. I purchased it to branch the water purifier hose without drilling any holes. 2. Brand: I understand this product is identical to the 2022 SK Mecha product, except for the logo, and every part is the same. Samsung, Coupang, and even the discontinued SK Mecha product all sell Media products via OEM, so it is a company I trust. Sentence (English): I purchased this dishwasher over a month ago.
Comments (English): [ Exceeded expectations! ] || ---------------- || I purchased this dishwasher over a month ago. I wanted to use it for awhile before reviewing it. The first few washes, I used the "tough" setting- result, clean sparkling dishes & DRY! Next few loads, used the prowash- result, clean sparkling dishes & DRY! Next few loads, I went to normal wash- left on foods, scraping dishes or wiping with paper towel. Result- clean, sparkling dishes & DRY! I Emphasize DRY! Even the plastic, which takes forever to dry. I do open it a 5-10 mins after it's done & either leave open a bit or hang a towel over the door & close it but not completly. Best feature is the top or first rack! Love being able to put small glasses, cups, whatever up there. Second, or middle rack adjusts up or down, even at an angle! Up for tall items on the bottom, down for tall items in that rack. The glides or rollers are so smooth & fast- if not careful, you'd think they would fly out of the thing if you pull it out too quickly!

Sentence (English): Decided to make this purchase after doing research and comparisons.
Comments (English): [ Good cleaning power - bad functionality ] || ---------------- || Decided to make this purchase after doing research and comparisons. After using it for a few weeks, yes the cleaning cycles are strong and don't underwhelm in any way, but I'm very disappointed with a few key things. First off - I was very disappointed to learn this model does not have the red timing light shining on the floor. Almost every other model I researched has the feature. When I chose to upgrade my purchase from the 500 model to the 800 model - I didn't think I'd get LESS features. Second - there is no way to know if the dang machine is done! Yes, I have it hooked up to my cell phone and I get the notification. We run the dishwasher just before bed. I get 10-12 notifications overnight and the message from Bosch about my dishwasher finishing its cycle is easily lost. When my wife wakes up, who doesn't get the notifications, she has no clue whether it ran or not. Simple fix - make the LED on the door turn red when it's running and turn white when it's done (light goes out when the door is opened). Third - I hate that I have to use the app to delay a cycle. Just put a button on the machine for delay - 1 hr, 2 hr, 3 hr, 4 hr. And speaking of buttons, they are not very responsive - I find myself needing to push a button 3-4 times before it beeps. These are simple functions that even the cheapest dishwashers do - and do well. I think Bosch is paying way too much attention to fashion and has lost sight on functionality. If I could return it - I would. Do better.

After using it for a few weeks, yes the cleaning cycles are strong and don't underwhelm in any way, but I'm very disappointed with a few key things. First off - I was very disappointed to learn this model does not have the red timing light shining on the floor. Almost every other model I researched has the feature. When I chose to upgrade my purchase from the 500 model to the 800 model - I didn't think I'd get LESS features. Second - there is no way to know if the dang machine is done! Yes, I have it hooked up to my cell phone and I get the notification. We run the dishwasher just before bed. I get 10-12 notifications overnight and the message from Bosch about my dishwasher finishing its cycle is easily lost. When my wife wakes up, who doesn't get the notifications, she has no clue whether it ran or not. Simple fix - make the LED on the door turn red when it's running and turn white when it's done (light goes out when the door is opened). Third - I hate that I have to use the app to delay a cycle. Just put a button on the machine for delay - 1 hr, 2 hr, 3 hr, 4 hr. And speaking of buttons, they are not very responsive - I find myself needing to push a button 3-4 times before it beeps. These are simple functions that even the cheapest dishwashers do - and do well. I think Bosch is paying way too much attention to fashion and has lost sight on functionality. If I could return it - I would. Do better.

Comments (English): [ Installation and Haul-Away May Not Be Included ] || ---------------- || I purchased a new dishwasher online that was dropped off in our kitchen. The deliverers said they did not install the products, they just delivered them. After a week with no word about installation, I contacted Costco. The operator said it did not appear installation was included. I said that I specifically recalled the Costco webpage for appliances, in touting why you should purchase your appliances through Costco, states that delivery, installation, and haul-away are all included in the price. He said there may not be people in your area available to install the dishwasher. As a result I initiated a return and will now have to go to a local appliance retainer. I'm a huge Costco fan, having been a member who has shopped there weekly for the past 30 years. This is just an outlier, I guess. In any event, check to see if installation in available in your area before your order an appliance on-line through Costco.

Sentence (English): I was looking to buy a dishwasher when I saw that the price on Coupang had recently dropped to its lowest, so I bought it right away.
Comments (English): [ The design is pretty and the performance is good. ] || ---------------- || I was looking to buy a dishwasher when I saw that the price on Coupang had recently dropped to its lowest, so I bought it right away. I purchased it on Saturday and had it installed just two days later, on Monday. Coupang really does deliver appliances fast. On Sunday evening, the technician called to give me an approximate visit time and informed me that there might be an additional fee if any other installations were required. My house has an oven cabinet under the induction cooktop, so the structure requires removing the cabinet to fit the dishwasher. There was no separate installation fee for simply removing the cabinet to install the dishwasher. They called again on the day of the visit to schedule a time, and after completing the installation, they left after giving me a detailed explanation. Sentence (English): We're absolutely loving our new Bosch 500 Series dishwasher!
Comments (English): [ Quiet, Efficient, and Packed with Features – Love ] || ---------------- || We're absolutely loving our new Bosch 500 Series dishwasher! The separate third tray for silverware and small items is a game-changer—it saves so much space and keeps everything organized. Our favorite feature is the auto-open function at the end of the cycle, which speeds up drying and leaves the dishes spotless. One of the biggest surprises is just how quiet this dishwasher is! I really appreciate the small light that projects onto the floor to indicate whether it's running or paused (when it's blinking); otherwise, you'd barely notice it was on. Another unexpected favorite is the appliance app. I didn't think I'd need an app for a dishwasher, but it's been incredibly handy. It alerts me when the rinse-aid is low, lets me set favorite and remote control settings, and even helps me confirm if I remembered to resume the cycle after opening the door to add a dish. It's taken a bit of time to get used to not pre-rinsing the dishes like I did with my old dishwasher, but that's been a welcome change. I'm still perfecting my loading technique, but it cleans far better than my previous LG. This dishwasher has exceeded my expectations in so many ways. Highly recommend!

I love the DW- Costco installation? not so much. they have some room for improvement.

Sentence (English): The LG dishwasher that came as standard in my apartment was old and broken, so I replaced it with a Samsung Bespoke.
Comments (English): [ The LG dishwasher that came standard in my apartment was old and broke down, so I replaced it with a Samsung Bespoke. ] || ---------------- || The LG dishwasher that came as standard in my apartment was old and broken, so I replaced it with a Samsung Bespoke. It still makes a lot of water stains, but it's quiet, so I really like it. Before purchasing, I did a lot of research to see if I really needed a dryer function, and whether I should buy a 12-person or 14-person one. The bigger the better! Many people said that even with the hot air dryer, the electricity bill would be higher, and since I wouldn't necessarily use it, I would just use the standard setting, so I decided on the 14-person 800. The dishwasher had to have the mop holder cut before it was delivered, so a remodeler came and delivered it after remodeling. I really liked it because it was done in one day. Samsung technicians are always very kind. I feel at ease because my home appliances are being replaced one by one with Samsung products. Comments (English): This is an honest review of the Midea 6-seater countertop dishwasher. Hello! I'm a housewife in my 30s raising two sons. With both housework and childcare always busy, I finally bought a dishwasher to help with the dishes. Using the Midea 6-seater countertop dishwasher has truly improved my quality of life. I just put a spoon with rice cake stuck to it in the dishwasher as a test, and the results were fantastic! Sentence (English): I live alone but enjoy cooking at home, so I've always had a lot of concerns about dishwashers.
Comments (English): I live alone but enjoy cooking at home, so I've always had a lot of concerns about dishwashers. I always found something lacking: the design was unsatisfactory, the size was too small or too large, or the controls were cumbersome. The Midea dishwasher seemed to meet all my criteria, so I chose it. After using it for a few days, here are my impressions: 1. It has a beautiful design. I'm a looker who prioritizes design over performance, even when buying a car. The minimalist design and wooden handle detail were captivating enough for me. The ivory color is warm and understated, blending seamlessly into my home's surroundings. 2. It's easy to use. It operates with a single button, eliminating complex settings. For more detailed settings and management, a remote control app is available for easy access. 3. It performs exceptionally well. Even on the quick cycle, it thoroughly cleaned dishes stained with oil and seasoning. It removed most stains without needing to use the high speed. This was my favorite part. 4. Sentence (English): This is an honest review of the Midea 6-seater countertop dishwasher.
Comments (English): This is an honest review of the Midea 6-seater countertop dishwasher. Hello! I'm a housewife in my 30s raising two sons. With constant housework and childcare, I finally bought a dishwasher to help with the dishes. Using the Midea 6-seater countertop dishwasher has truly improved my quality of life. I'll share my honest thoughts from using it and the results of additional testing. What I liked: 1. App integration. I found it incredibly convenient to be able to check the washing process and adjust settings from my smartphone. I can even control the washing cycle with the app, so I no longer have to worry about forgetting to do the dishes while putting the kids to bed. 2. Auto door open. I really liked how the door automatically opens after the wash cycle is over, allowing moisture to escape and drying the dishes. Even greasy dishes dried cleanly, so I didn't have to worry about odors. 3. Spoon and rice paste test. You were most curious about whether the rice paste was completely removed, right? I just put a spoon with rice cake stuck to it in the dishwasher as a test, and the results were fantastic! The dishwasher's cleaning power was excellent, and it washed the rice cake cleanly, leaving no trace. 4. Lunchbox Oil Test. I also put a plastic lunchbox that I'd used to hold greasy side dishes in. Washing it by hand often leaves behind a greasy residue, right? But when I ran it through this dishwasher, it was squeaky clean! Not a single oil stain left. I was especially relieved that the plastic bowls didn't discolor. 5. Compact Size. It's a good size for even a small kitchen, making it easy to utilize the space. My family of four runs it once a day, and the capacity was just right. Cons: 1. Capacity limitations. It's designed for six people, so it's difficult to fit large pots and pans. It might be a bit small for frequent cooks or guests. 2. Insufficient manual. The installation and app integration instructions were a bit sparse. I found some troubleshooting tips on YouTube, but it might be a bit cumbersome for first-time users. Overall Review: I highly recommend the Media Dishwasher to busy housewives with children and chores. Especially, the cleaning power, which removes even the greasy residue from spoons, rice grime, and lunch boxes, has significantly reduced the stress of dishwashing. Smart features like app integration and automatic door opening are also incredibly convenient. Rating: (4.5/5). Would I buy it again? Absolutely! Stop wasting time on dishes and spend more time with your family! This is an honest review written after receiving the product as part of the Coupang Experience Group.
Comments (Original): 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료 제공받아 작성한 리뷰입니다.미디어 6인용 카운터탑 식기세척기 솔직 리뷰안녕하세요! 아들 둘 키우는 30대 주부입니다. 집안일도 육아도 늘 바쁘다 보니 설거지를 도와줄 식기세척기를 드디어 들였어요. 미디어(Midea) 6인용 카운터탑 식기세척기를 사용해 보니 정말 삶의 질이 올라간 느낌이에요. 제가 직접 사용하면서 느낀 점들, 그리고 추가로 테스트해본 결과까지 솔직하게 공유해 볼게요.좋았던 점1. 앱 연동 기능스마트폰으로 세척 상태를 확인하거나 설정을 바꿀 수 있는 기능이 진짜 편했어요. 설거지 시작도 앱으로 조작할 수 있어서 아이들 재우다 까먹은 설거지 걱정도 줄었어요.2. 자동 문 열림 기능세척이 끝나면 문이 자동으로 열려서 습기가 빠지면서 건조까지 알아서 되는 게 정말 좋았어요. 기름기 많은 그릇도 산뜻하게 건조되어 냄새 걱정이 없더라고요.3. 수저 밥풀 테스트밥풀 말끔히 씻기는지 가장 궁금하셨죠? 테스트 삼아 밥풀을 붙인 수저를 그냥 넣었는데 결과는 대만족! 세척력이 좋아서 밥풀이 흔적도 없이 깨끗하게 씻기더라고요.4. 반찬통 기름 테스트기름진 반찬을 담았던 플라스틱 반찬통도 한번 넣어봤어요. 손으로 닦으면 기름기가 남는 경우가 많잖아요? 그런데 이 식기세척기로 돌리니 뽀득뽀득! 기름 자국 하나 없이 깔끔했어요. 특히 플라스틱 그릇이 변색되지 않아서 안심했답니다.5. 컴팩트한 크기작은 주방에도 부담 없이 놓을 수 있는 크기라 공간 활용도 좋아요. 우리 가족은 4인인데 하루 한 번씩 돌리기에 용량이 딱 맞더라고요.아쉬운 점1. 용량의 한계6인용이라 큰 냄비나 프라이팬은 넣기 어렵더라고요. 요리 자주 하시거나 손님 맞이용으로는 조금 작을 수 있어요.2. 설명서 부족설치랑 앱 연동 설명이 조금 부족했어요. 저는 유튜브 찾아보며 해결했는데, 처음 쓰는 분들에겐 번거로울 수도 있을 것 같아요.총평미디어 식기세척기는 육아와 집안일에 바쁜 주부들에게 정말 추천하고 싶은 제품이에요. 특히 수저 밥풀이나 반찬통의 기름기도 문제없이 씻기는 세척력 덕분에 설거지 스트레스가 확 줄었답니다. 앱 연동이나 자동 문 열림 같은 스마트 기능도 정말 편리하고요.별점: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4.5/5)다시 사겠냐고요? 무조건이죠!설거지로 시간 뺏기지 말고 가족들과 더 많은 시간을 보내세요!쿠팡체험단으로 제품을 제공받아 솔직하게 작성하는 리뷰입니다.

Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Sentence (English): I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes.
Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

심지어 혈육이 삼* 직원이라 지금 이 모델과 같은 스펙인 삼*꺼 식세기를 30만원가량 저렴하게 살 수 있는 상황이지만 좋은게 좋은거겠지하고 LG꺼 이 모델로 결정했습니다.이 모델을 구매하기로 결정하고 가을즈음 부터 가격 추이를 지켜봤는데 쿠팡내에서 하루이틀 사이에도 가격변동이 심하더라고요.지켜보다가 갑자기 가격이 훅 떨어지는 날에 구매했습니다.배송/설치는 Sentence (English): My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids.
Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Sentence (English): Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall.
Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!
