Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Sentence (English): Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea.
Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Sentence (English): The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher.
Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Sentence (English): This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage.
Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Sentence (English): Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!
Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

Sentence (English): Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!
Comments (English): I bought this LG dishwasher because it has a 10cm dish rack among the 14-person models. Until four years ago, when I was a family of three, we used a S Magic 6-person dishwasher that sits on top of the sink. But after cooking dinner for three family members, the dishwasher was too cramped to fit all the dishes and pots and pans in it. So, I hand-washed the bulky pots and pans separately and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Eventually, playing Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher became too much of a hassle, so I started washing everything by hand and the dishwasher became relegated to just serving as a dish rack. Then, I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher altogether, just washing dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born. With a newborn and the need to take my first child to and from school and pick them up from their academy, I was so busy that I didn't have the time or energy to do the dishes, and my wrists were hurting. My husband tells me to save the dishes for later in the day since he'll do the dishes after dinner. But if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, and so on, they pile up like a mountain in the sink. I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. Even though I'm busy, I make time to wash them. I wash my hands countless times a day, using detergent, and washing dishes. Now, not only do I have housewife eczema, but I'm also getting some kind of skin condition on the backs of my hands. Wearing rubber gloves makes it worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without a word, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for nearly an hour doing them, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my eldest son with his homework and look after my newborn. Dinnertime flies by in a flash. Dinner is the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but since dishwashing reduces our time together, I knew I absolutely needed a dishwasher, so I started looking around fall. I compared LG and Samsung models with similar specs and a 10cm dishwasher base. The key differences were that Samsung's had a water filter and was not manufactured in Korea. LG's had the advantage of a True Steam function, but unlike Samsung's, it required adding salt and was manufactured in Korea. Ten years ago, when I got married, I was taught to trust LG as my go-to white goods, so I bought all my wedding appliances from LG. However, the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all developed defects and had to be serviced. Four years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option (not a custom-made one), but the drain pump was defective and started leaking. One night, I was sleeping when water leaked from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling. Two years ago, I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, but I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common-sense (?) that you absolutely must buy an LG TV. But this summer, two years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs. To that extent, our family has had enough of these issues with LG appliances that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with Samsung products. I was worried that the LG dishwasher would break again when it arrived at our house. Nevertheless, we chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Samsung employee mall, and since we're related to a Samsung employee, we could get a Samsung dishwasher with the same specs for about 300,000 won cheaper, but I figured better is better, so I decided on this LG model. I decided to buy this model and started monitoring the price around fall. I noticed that prices on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. I watched for a while, and then suddenly the price dropped, so I bought it. An LG technician came and did the delivery and installation. My sink cabinet is a 600mm standard, so I could just remove the cabinets, but I had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, which cost an additional 80,000 won. Having used a 6-seater dishwasher until a few years ago, I'm familiar with the dish Tetris and pre-washing methods, so I have no problems using this one. The dish Tetris method is something you learn over time. For the pre-washing method, after you're done eating, you just throw away the food and rinse it with water. By submerging it in a large bowl filled with water, you can remove most of the food without having to use a scrubber. It's definitely much more spacious than my previous 6-seater dishwasher, so I don't have to worry about the Tetris game of trying to cram dishes into the small space. The extra space means you can just place everything in the dishwasher. It's the same size as my older 12-seater model with two baskets. This 14-person dishwasher features three baskets, offering ample dish storage. The downside is that while it's more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, it uses more electricity and requires bending down to load them. Still, it's a life-changing experience, so I highly recommend it to anyone considering buying one. Buy it now and be free from the hassle of washing dishes!

I would definitely recommend this unit.

Comments (English): [ Quite a Looker and Quiet Performer ] || ---------------- || When I walked into your appliance area and saw Kyle, a 25-yr old salesman sitting there, I thought to myself that there's no way this kid knows the first thing about dishwashers. The Lg was spot-on and he had to have noticed my surprise! He deserves a raise! Impressive. On to the the LG. My parameters were: no 3rd rack. This LG is very quiet and to get a DW this quiet in other brands, you must pay nearly twice as much as I paid for the LG. Stainless-steel interior is perfect and installation was very easy. LG cleans the dirtiest dishes with ease, and I never have to pre-rinse anything. Overall, I'd recommend this unit to anyone who appreciates value paired with common-sense features and performance….and yes, it's definitely for those who relish quiet.

Sentence (English): I don't love the Bosch 800 series like I hoped I would.
Comments (English): [ Bosch 800: Not loving it. ] || ---------------- || I don't love the Bosch 800 series like I hoped I would. After the first load, we didn't open the door right away, and the some of our dishes and glasses had areas of what appeared to be black mold. The moisture in the DW while the door was shut evidently caused this. Not good at all. It is a bother to have to prop the door open after each load to avoid moldy dishes. And I got the handle so I could hang a towel…It does not look good w/the door always propped open. PLUS, the tynes are angled so the way you have to put the dishes & cups angled so water runs off them. But this is an awkward & quite different way to load. Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ At first, when I used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because there weren't any dishes washed;;; I just found out that stacking dishes in a dishwasher is extremely important. . I think it gets the cleanest when you set it up at an angle. I've been using it for a long time and now I'm a veteran~ But sometimes, if I put too much in, one or two dishes don't get cleaned. Light plastic things (rice containers) keep flipping over in the water, so after washing them, the rice container is full of dishwater;;;;; You have to put them in carefully so that they don't flip over. Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ At first, when I used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because there weren't any dishes washed;;; I just found out that stacking dishes in a dishwasher is extremely important. . Sentence (English): I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because not a single dish was washed;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important when using a dishwasher. .
Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because not a single dish was washed;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important when using a dishwasher. . I think it gets the cleanest when you set it up slanted. I've been using it for a while and now I'm a veteran~ But sometimes, if I put too much in, one or two dishes won't be cleaned. Light plastic things (rice containers) keep flipping over in the water, so after washing, the rice container is full of dishwater;;;;; You have to put it in carefully so that it doesn't flip over. I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried that the electricity bill will be high, so I only use the standard course these days~ That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes are not dry at all and they're not crispy. They say this is the same for other brands. It would be better if the door automatically opens and dries the dishes after they are washed. Since they were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it doesn't need to be dried. The noise is a little humming when the water drains, and it's not that loud when it runs. It's not very quiet. If you run it in the evening, the dishes will be dry in the morning, which is nice. ^^ I think there are some products that you shouldn't put in. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I threw something in without knowing (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Spoons with a wide grip don't fit in the spoon holder. Children's spoons usually have rounded parts made of characters or plastic. Those kinds of things can't be inserted because the holes are small. And if you just throw them away, the holes in the dishwasher are too big for them to fall out. But I never give up and just place them gently on the spoon holder. ^^ When I put them all together, it feels like the sink counter is getting dirtier. It washes away hardened rice paste well though~ When you buy a dishwasher, you should also buy a solid dishwasher detergent~ I just bought a dishwasher and wanted to use it quickly, but it said I needed a solid detergent so I was able to use it the next day~~ They say that the product specifications are similar except for the brand (according to the installer). I also get a little stressed out by the dish Tetris, but I am satisfied and using it well~ Some people said that they haven't washed dishes since buying a dishwasher. It's not as convenient as a dryer, but after using it, it has become something I can't live without~ That's the end of the real real review~~~~~

Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because not a single dish was washed;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important when using a dishwasher. . I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried that the electricity bill will be high, so I only use the standard course these days~ That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes are not dry at all and they're not crispy. They say this is the same for other brands. It would be better if the door automatically opens and dries the dishes after they are washed. Since they were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it doesn't need to be dried. The noise is a little humming when the water drains, and it's not that loud when it runs. It's not very quiet. If you run it in the evening, the dishes will be dry in the morning, which is nice. ^^ I think there are some products that you shouldn't put in. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I threw something in without knowing (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Spoons with a wide grip don't fit in the spoon holder. Children's spoons usually have rounded parts made of characters or plastic. Those kinds of things can't be inserted because the holes are small. Sentence (English): I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function.
Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because not a single dish was washed;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important when using a dishwasher. . Light plastic things (rice containers) keep flipping over in the water, so after washing, the rice container is full of dishwater;;;;; You have to put it in carefully so that it doesn't flip over. I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried that the electricity bill will be high, so I only use the standard course these days~ That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes are not dry at all and they're not crispy. They say this is the same for other brands. It would be better if the door automatically opens and dries the dishes after they are washed. Since they were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it doesn't need to be dried. The noise is a little humming when the water drains, and it's not that loud when it runs. It's not very quiet. If you run it in the evening, the dishes will be dry in the morning, which is nice. ^^ I think there are some products that you shouldn't put in. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I threw something in without knowing (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Spoons with a wide grip don't fit in the spoon holder. Children's spoons usually have rounded parts made of characters or plastic. Those kinds of things can't be inserted because the holes are small. Sentence (English): It's not very quiet.
Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because not a single dish was washed;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important when using a dishwasher. . Light plastic things (rice containers) keep flipping over in the water, so after washing, the rice container is full of dishwater;;;;; You have to put it in carefully so that it doesn't flip over. I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried that the electricity bill will be high, so I only use the standard course these days~ That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes are not dry at all and they're not crispy. They say this is the same for other brands. It would be better if the door automatically opens and dries the dishes after they are washed. Since they were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it doesn't need to be dried. The noise is a little humming when the water drains, and it's not that loud when it runs. It's not very quiet. If you run it in the evening, the dishes will be dry in the morning, which is nice. ^^ I think there are some products that you shouldn't put in. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I threw something in without knowing (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Spoons with a wide grip don't fit in the spoon holder. Children's spoons usually have rounded parts made of characters or plastic. Those kinds of things can't be inserted because the holes are small. Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because not a single dish was washed;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important when using a dishwasher. . Light plastic things (rice containers) keep flipping over in the water, so after washing, the rice container is full of dishwater;;;;; You have to put it in carefully so that it doesn't flip over. I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried that the electricity bill will be high, so I only use the standard course these days~ That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes are not dry at all and they're not crispy. They say this is the same for other brands. It would be better if the door automatically opens and dries the dishes after they are washed. Since they were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it doesn't need to be dried. The noise is a little humming when the water drains, and it's not that loud when it runs. It's not very quiet. If you run it in the evening, the dishes will be dry in the morning, which is nice. ^^ I think there are some products that you shouldn't put in. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I threw something in without knowing (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Spoons with a wide grip don't fit in the spoon holder. Children's spoons usually have rounded parts made of characters or plastic. Those kinds of things can't be inserted because the holes are small. Sentence (English): I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because it didn't wash a single dish;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important for a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because it didn't wash a single dish;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important for a dishwasher. I think it gets the cleanest when you set it up at an angle. I've been using it for a while and now I'm a veteran~. But sometimes, if I put too many in, one or two dishes won't be cleaned. Light things like plastic (rice containers) keep flipping over in the water, so when you look after the dishes are done, the rice container is full of dishwashing water;;;;; You have to put it in carefully so that it doesn't flip over. I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried about the electricity bill, so I only use the standard course these days. That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes aren't dry at all and they're not crispy. I heard that this is the same with other brands. It's better when the door automatically opens and dries them after they're done washing. Since the dishes were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it's not necessary to dry them. The noise is a little humming when the water drains, and it's not that loud when it runs. It's not very quiet. If I run it in the evening, the dishes are dry in the morning, which is nice^^. It seems like there are products that you shouldn't put in. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I accidentally threw something in it (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Kids with wide spoon grips won't fit in the spoon holder. Children's spoons usually have rounded parts made of character or plastic. Those kinds of things can't be inserted because the holes are small. But if you just throw them, the holes in the dishwasher are too big, so they all fall out. But I never give up and just place them gently on the spoon holder^^. Since I put them all together, the sink seems to get dirtier. It still washes away things like hardened rice paste well~ When you buy a dishwasher, you should also buy solid dishwasher detergent~ I just bought a dishwasher and wanted to use it quickly, but they said it needed solid detergent, so I was able to use it the next day~~ They say that the product specifications are similar except for the brand (what the installer said). I also find the dish Tetris a bit stressful, but I'm satisfied and using it well~ Some people even said that they haven't washed dishes once since getting a dishwasher. It's not as convenient as a dryer, but after using it, it's become something I can't live without~. That's the end of this really really really review~~~~~

Sentence (English): I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function.
Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because it didn't wash a single dish;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important for a dishwasher. I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried about the electricity bill, so I only use the standard course these days. That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes aren't dry at all and they're not crispy. I heard that this is the same with other brands. It's better when the door automatically opens and dries them after they're done washing. Since the dishes were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it's not necessary to dry them. It seems like there are products that you shouldn't put in. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I accidentally threw something in it (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Sentence (English): At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried about the electricity bill, so I only use the standard course these days.
Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because it didn't wash a single dish;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important for a dishwasher. I think it gets the cleanest when you set it up at an angle. I've been using it for a while and now I'm a veteran~. But sometimes, if I put too many in, one or two dishes won't be cleaned. Light things like plastic (rice containers) keep flipping over in the water, so when you look after the dishes are done, the rice container is full of dishwashing water;;;;; You have to put it in carefully so that it doesn't flip over. I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried about the electricity bill, so I only use the standard course these days. That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes aren't dry at all and they're not crispy. I heard that this is the same with other brands. It's better when the door automatically opens and dries them after they're done washing. Since the dishes were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it's not necessary to dry them. The noise is a little humming when the water drains, and it's not that loud when it runs. It's not very quiet. If I run it in the evening, the dishes are dry in the morning, which is nice^^. It seems like there are products that you shouldn't put in. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I accidentally threw something in it (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Kids with wide spoon grips won't fit in the spoon holder. Children's spoons usually have rounded parts made of character or plastic. Those kinds of things can't be inserted because the holes are small. But if you just throw them, the holes in the dishwasher are too big, so they all fall out. But I never give up and just place them gently on the spoon holder^^. Since I put them all together, the sink seems to get dirtier. It still washes away things like hardened rice paste well~ When you buy a dishwasher, you should also buy solid dishwasher detergent~ I just bought a dishwasher and wanted to use it quickly, but they said it needed solid detergent, so I was able to use it the next day~~ They say that the product specifications are similar except for the brand (what the installer said). I also find the dish Tetris a bit stressful, but I'm satisfied and using it well~ Some people even said that they haven't washed dishes once since getting a dishwasher. It's not as convenient as a dryer, but after using it, it's become something I can't live without~. That's the end of this really really really review~~~~~

Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because it didn't wash a single dish;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important for a dishwasher. Light things like plastic (rice containers) keep flipping over in the water, so when you look after the dishes are done, the rice container is full of dishwashing water;;;;; You have to put it in carefully so that it doesn't flip over. I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried about the electricity bill, so I only use the standard course these days. That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes aren't dry at all and they're not crispy. I heard that this is the same with other brands. It's better when the door automatically opens and dries them after they're done washing. Since the dishes were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it's not necessary to dry them. The noise is a little humming when the water drains, and it's not that loud when it runs. It's not very quiet. If I run it in the evening, the dishes are dry in the morning, which is nice^^. It seems like there are products that you shouldn't put in. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I accidentally threw something in it (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Kids with wide spoon grips won't fit in the spoon holder. Children's spoons usually have rounded parts made of character or plastic. Those kinds of things can't be inserted because the holes are small. But if you just throw them, the holes in the dishwasher are too big, so they all fall out. It's not as convenient as a dryer, but after using it, it's become something I can't live without~. That's the end of this really really really review~~~~~

Sentence (English): It's not very quiet.
Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because it didn't wash a single dish;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important for a dishwasher. I think it gets the cleanest when you set it up at an angle. I've been using it for a while and now I'm a veteran~. But sometimes, if I put too many in, one or two dishes won't be cleaned. Light things like plastic (rice containers) keep flipping over in the water, so when you look after the dishes are done, the rice container is full of dishwashing water;;;;; You have to put it in carefully so that it doesn't flip over. I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried about the electricity bill, so I only use the standard course these days. That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes aren't dry at all and they're not crispy. I heard that this is the same with other brands. It's better when the door automatically opens and dries them after they're done washing. Since the dishes were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it's not necessary to dry them. The noise is a little humming when the water drains, and it's not that loud when it runs. It's not very quiet. If I run it in the evening, the dishes are dry in the morning, which is nice^^. It seems like there are products that you shouldn't put in. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I accidentally threw something in it (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Kids with wide spoon grips won't fit in the spoon holder. Children's spoons usually have rounded parts made of character or plastic. Those kinds of things can't be inserted because the holes are small. But if you just throw them, the holes in the dishwasher are too big, so they all fall out. But I never give up and just place them gently on the spoon holder^^. Since I put them all together, the sink seems to get dirtier. It still washes away things like hardened rice paste well~ When you buy a dishwasher, you should also buy solid dishwasher detergent~ I just bought a dishwasher and wanted to use it quickly, but they said it needed solid detergent, so I was able to use it the next day~~ They say that the product specifications are similar except for the brand (what the installer said). I also find the dish Tetris a bit stressful, but I'm satisfied and using it well~ Some people even said that they haven't washed dishes once since getting a dishwasher. It's not as convenient as a dryer, but after using it, it's become something I can't live without~. That's the end of this really really really review~~~~~

Comments (English): [ Freestanding installation ] || ---------------- || I installed it freestanding~ It's possible as long as there's a place for water to drain~ When I first used it without knowing anything, I was surprised because it didn't wash a single dish;;; I just found out that stacking dishes is incredibly important for a dishwasher. I thought there was no drying function, but there is a drying function. Turn on the power, press the standard course once, and press the dry once. It takes 2 hours, and the standard course alone takes about an hour. At first, I kept using the dry function, but I'm worried about the electricity bill, so I only use the standard course these days. That's because even when I press the dry function, the dishes aren't dry at all and they're not crispy. I heard that this is the same with other brands. It's better when the door automatically opens and dries them after they're done washing. Since the dishes were washed in very hot water anyway, I think it's not necessary to dry them. Glass can break if you're not careful, and I panicked when I accidentally threw something in it (a child's spoon bag) and it shrunk and broke. And the spoon holder is a bit inconvenient for me. Sentence (English): No more power after having this machine for about 3-4 years.
Comments (English): [ Just Don't Buy GE ] || ---------------- || No more power after having this machine for about 3-4 years. Called GE customer care and they said there's no similar issues reported on this machine, while there are plenty here in the review. Watched another YouTube video of a guy trying to fix his GE dishwasher with identical issues by replacing the main control board and I took my control board off of the machine. There were obvious fume marks on the plastic backing of the main control board so I decided to call GE to buy a replacement board. The rep said the part number printed on the control board is not how they are captured in their system, and all the p/n in their system starts with "W" and the board I held in my hand doesn't even have a 'W' anywhere. Double checked the model number and it's the main control board, I asked the rep to place the order for me. Then it turned out it's indeed another main control board for another machine! The connectors housing shape is different, pin number is different. I'm doubting whether GE has a good system for field service parts. The cost of the board was about $100 new from GE. Maybe just buy another brand entirely is the best option now.
